tasks.prompt: Write a plain JavaScript (CommonJS, no imports) function `chunk(arr, size)` that splits the array `arr` into consecutive sub-arrays of length `size` (the last one may be shorter). It must not mutate `arr`. If `size` is not a positive integer, throw a RangeError. Output ONLY the code, no explanation.

Write a TypeScript function `export function parseRange(spec: string): number[]` that parses a page-range spec like "1-3,5,8-9" into a sorted array of unique integers [1,2,3,5,8,9]. Whitespace around items is allowed. An empty string returns []. Any malformed item (e.g. "a", "3-1", "1-") must throw an Error. Use explicit types; no `any`. Output ONLY the code, no explanation.

A JavaScript function `slugify(s)` is ALREADY defined and in scope (do not define or require it). Spec: it lowercases the string, trims it, replaces every run of characters that are not a-z or 0-9 with a single hyphen, and removes leading/trailing hyphens; e.g. slugify("  Hello, World! ") === "hello-world" and slugify("A--B") === "a-b". Write at least 4 test assertions for it using Node's built-in `assert` module (`const assert = require("assert");`), as a plain script (no test framework). Output ONLY the code, no explanation.
